fixtures.preview: Michael Carrick's United travel to Madrid for matchday 2 of the Champions League league phase, needing a response after a poor start to the season.
talking_points: United drew 1-1 with Spurs on Saturday (Mbeumo 73', Solanke 90+2'), leaving them with their fewest points after six league games since 1986-87, per Sky Sports.
They are on a four-match winless run and have won only two of their eight games this season, per the Racing Post.
Sesko, Dorgu, de Ligt and Ugarte are reported injured and Mazraoui is a doubt; the Racing Post's line-ups are predictions, not confirmed.
Atlético are unbeaten in four LaLiga games, took 10 points from 12 at home and are narrow favourites (10-11 with Sky Bet); United's Carlos Baleba made his debut off the bench against Spurs.

fixtures.preview: A Sunday 2pm Roses clash at Elland Road, with seventh-placed Leeds (9 points) hosting 13th-placed United (6 points) on NBC Sports' table.
A trip to Lake Como for matchday 3 of the Champions League league phase.
Sunday home game against Bournemouth, who are 17th on 3 points, moved from Saturday for UK TV.
Lunchtime trip to Stamford Bridge to face sixth-placed Chelsea (10 points).
The first season-opening Sydney Derby in A-League history, with both clubs under new head coaches and a capacity crowd expected.
talking_points: Ufuk Talay, Sydney FC's former coach, takes charge of the Wanderers in his first A-League match against his old club.
Sydney FC lead the head-to-head 22 wins to 12 (10 draws) and won the last meeting 2-0 at CommBank Stadium in April.
Sydney FC are without striker Victor Campuzano (ACL, out for the season); new loan signing Oriola Sunday has taken his No. 9 shirt.
The Wanderers' new faces include Miguel Di Pizio, Panashe Madanha, Liam Gillion and Germán Ferreyra, with Brandon Borrello the new captain.

fixtures.preview: A family-friendly Sunday-afternoon home game against Adelaide United.
Halloween-day 5pm away game at AAMI Park, Melbourne City's home opener.
Friday-night home game against the Mariners; the date comes from fixture listings and the kick-off isn't confirmed by the club.
Round 5 away trip to Brisbane Roar at Kayo Stadium.

big_matches.title: Manchester City v Paris Saint-Germain
big_matches.why: Heavyweights meet at the Etihad, with Pep Guardiola reportedly set to return as a visitor.
talking_points: Premier League leaders City are unbeaten under Enzo Maresca; PSG won 6-1 on matchday one.
Erling Haaland, Antoine Semenyo and Nico O'Reilly are doubts for City, while Phil Foden is available.
PSG's Ousmane Dembélé is reportedly racing to be fit, with Neves, Nuno Mendes and Marquinhos also carrying fitness concerns.

big_matches.title: Wallabies v All Blacks (Bledisloe Cup)
big_matches.why: The Cup is already gone after a 50-19 loss at Eden Park, so Les Kiss's Wallabies need a response at Accor Stadium.

big_matches.title: Paris Saint-Germain v Barcelona
big_matches.why: Two of Europe's most attacking sides meet in matchday 3.

big_matches.title: Bayern Munich v Arsenal
big_matches.why: Arsenal, second in the Premier League, visit the Allianz Arena on matchday 3.

big_matches.title: Barcelona v Real Madrid (El Clásico)
big_matches.why: First Clásico of the season at Camp Nou; beIN Sports shows every LaLiga match in Australia.
talking_points: It is billed as an early litmus test of both clubs' title credentials.
Barcelona top LaLiga on 24 points from eight games, while sources put Real Madrid on 16 to 18 points in third or fourth.
José Mourinho's Real Madrid travel to Camp Nou for this LaLiga matchday 10 fixture.

big_matches.title: Liverpool v Arsenal
big_matches.why: Second-placed Arsenal visit Anfield, moved to Sunday for TV.
talking_points: Arsenal are second on 15 points, behind Manchester City on 18, per NBC Sports' 11 October table.
Liverpool are ninth on 9 points, so Anfield is a chance to close the gap.

notes: Man Utd: the 1-1 draw with Spurs (10 Oct) is confirmed by Sky Sports; Carrick is the manager. The Atlético injury list comes from the Racing Post's predicted team news, so it is unconfirmed. Standings are from NBC Sports' 11 Oct table, and sources disagree on United's points total (5 or 6).

Sydney FC: the derby is 7:45pm per the club (other sources say 8pm). The Mariners date (6 Nov) is from fixture listings only and wasn't on the club's home-ticket list, so its kick-off is unconfirmed (listings suggest 7:40pm). Paramount+ shows every A-League Men match.

Big matches: no 2026 team news was found for PSG v Barcelona or Bayern v Arsenal, so they have no talking points. Liverpool v Man City (11 Oct) has finished and was dropped. The Man City v PSG notes come from a preview blog, not an official source.

Live sport: kick-off times for the Kings, volleyball and Flames games weren't published on the pages found. No Matildas, Socceroos, tennis or Waratahs home games were found in Sydney for the next four weeks.
Local: only two items found. No Term 4 events were found for the schools, nothing new at South Eveleigh or Sydney Park, and no local news from the last 7 days.

Not found this run: Pokémon, Minecraft or Roblox events, kids' fun runs beyond Triathlon Pink, matcha pop-ups, and Sydney author events. Rebel's Mid Season Sale ended 11 Oct and was removed. Crows Nest Fest (18 Oct) and Good Food Month events couldn't be confirmed from their pages.

Groceries: Woolworths and Coles specials are from the 7–13 Oct half-price trackers, so they end tomorrow, and several are brand ranges rather than exact items. New specials start Wed 14 Oct, and Aldi's specials couldn't be read.
